meta.titre: Mbida's First Cameroonian Government of 1957: formation, limits and end
meta.sous_theme: The first internal self-government of French Cameroon, 1957 to 1958

sections.contenu_markdown: In 1957 French Cameroon, for the first time, had a government led by a Cameroonian prime minister. Until then the French High Commissioner held the real authority. The new government came from the Assembly chosen in December 1956 and it lasted only a short time. Examiners often put a table of election results in front of you and ask which parties formed the government and who led it. This course shows you what to learn and how to read such a question.

items: The Legislative Assembly of Cameroon (ALCAM) was elected in December 1956 after the Loi Cadre.
A prime minister leads the government and is chosen from the Assembly.
Internal self-government means a territory manages its own domestic affairs while another power keeps control of key matters.

sections.titre: How the first self-government of French Cameroon worked
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The facts to know

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| What was formed in 1957? | The first internal self-government of French Cameroon, under a new statute |
| Who led it? | André-Marie Mbida, the first Prime Minister |
| Where did it come from? | From the ALCAM, elected in December 1956 |
| Who succeeded Mbida? | Ahidjo, in February 1958 |
| What came next? | Independence on 1 January 1960 |

### How the government was formed

After the elections the Assembly had members from several parties, and no single group could rule without allies. The Prime Minister was chosen from the Assembly and formed a government of ministers from the parties that supported him. Learn from your textbook the names of the parties in the Assembly. In an examination question the results table will be printed, so read the names of the parties from the table and write exactly the number asked.

### Powers and limits

The government managed local matters. France kept defence and foreign affairs and the High Commissioner remained its representative. The UPC, banned in 1955, was outside the system.

### Policy and end

Mbida favoured a slow movement to independence and worked closely with France. Many Cameroonians wanted faster change and reunification with the British Cameroons. Many historians say that disagreements within his government and loss of support in the Assembly led to the end of his government in early 1958. Ahidjo then became prime minister.

### Importance

It was the first time that Cameroonians held government posts at the head of the territory. It trained political leaders and prepared the way for independence.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a table of results is printed and the question asks for parties
variantes.contenu_markdown: Take the names from the table only. Choose parties with seats and write exactly the number asked, for example two. Do not add names from memory that are not asked for.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked who led the first government
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write André-Marie Mbida and the title Prime Minister. Do not write Ahidjo, who came after him, or leaders from the British Southern Cameroons.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to assess or discuss
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the achievement (first Cameroonian-led government) and the weaknesses (limits set by France, disagreement about independence, a short life). Finish with a judgement.

sections.enonce_markdown: Describe the first internal self-government of French Cameroon in 1957 and explain its importance. [8 marks]

etapes.justification: "Describe" asks for facts, "explain its importance" asks for reasons.
Facts about who and how score first.
etapes.resultat_markdown: It came from the Assembly elected in December 1956; Mbida was chosen Prime Minister under the 1957 statute.

etapes.justification: The examiner expects you to know that it was not independence.
etapes.resultat_markdown: France kept defence and foreign affairs and the High Commissioner remained.

etapes.justification: Importance means what difference it made.
etapes.resultat_markdown: It was the first government led by a Cameroonian and it trained leaders for independence.

etapes.action: Close with the end of the government.
etapes.justification: A closing fact completes the story.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Mbida was replaced by Ahidjo in February 1958.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The first internal self-government of French Cameroon was formed in 1957 from the Legislative Assembly elected in December 1956. André-Marie Mbida was the first Prime Minister. The government managed local affairs, but France kept defence and foreign affairs and the High Commissioner remained its representative. The government was important because Cameroonians for the first time led the territory's government, and it trained politicians for independence. It ended in February 1958 when Ahidjo replaced Mbida.

items.erreur_markdown: Ahidjo was the first head of the self-government.
items.pourquoi_faux: Ahidjo became prime minister after Mbida in 1958.
France kept key powers and independence came in 1960.
items.correction_markdown: Say that it was internal self-government only.

items.erreur_markdown: The leader was Foncha or Endeley.
items.pourquoi_faux: They led the British Southern Cameroons, not French Cameroon.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing four parties when two were asked.
items.pourquoi_faux: Extra names waste time and may be marked wrong.
items.correction_markdown: Write exactly the number requested, taken from the table.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that the UPC took part in the government.
items.correction_markdown: State that the UPC was banned and outside the system.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the first Prime Minister of French Cameroon under internal self-government and the year it began.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each. **André-Marie Mbida; 1957.**

items.enonce_markdown: Give two reasons why internal self-government in 1957 was not full independence.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for two reasons. France kept defence and foreign affairs. The High Commissioner remained its representative. **Independence came only on 1 January 1960.**

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss the achievements and weaknesses of the first self-government of French Cameroon. [10 marks]
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for both. Achievements: first Cameroonian-led government, training for independence, experience in governing. Weaknesses: limited powers, UPC outside the system, disagreement about independence, short life ending in February 1958. **Judgement: a useful but limited step.**

items_markdown: The first self-government of French Cameroon began in 1957 under Prime Minister André-Marie Mbida.
It came from the ALCAM elected in December 1956.
France kept defence and foreign affairs; the UPC was banned.
Ahidjo replaced Mbida in February 1958; independence came on 1 January 1960.
For party names, read the results table in the question and give exactly the number asked.
Do not confuse Mbida with leaders of the British Southern Cameroons.
